history.headline: Today's 21 km at easy pace and low effort marks the return of longer time-on-feet the strain flag was waiting for.
watch_items: Whether this longer run pulls the strain ratio back up, confirming the earlier dip was a rolling-average artefact.
Whether pack-loaded or back-to-back running finally appears, given how close the self-supported crossing now is.
Whether per-run elevation starts climbing to rehearse the sustained border-section terrain.
Whether the recent erratic nights settle into something steadier now that longer sessions are re-entering the week.

history.headline: A 12 km moderate run at controlled HR follows yesterday's long effort, capping a level four-week block heading into taper territory.
watch_items: Whether pack-loaded running finally enters the schedule, since the general base is ready but the specific weighted demand still isn't trained.
Whether climbing per run starts trending toward sustained ascent rather than the rolling profiles logged so far.
Whether the short-sleep nights begin clustering as longer efforts continue, rather than alternating with long-sleep nights.

history.headline: Easy-run HR holds well below the prior block into the recovery week, strengthening the case for a real efficiency gain.
watch_items: Whether the lower easy-run HR survives the return to higher volume — the confirming test for this efficiency gain.
Whether pack-carry running enters the schedule while there's still time to adapt the carry demand before the coast-to-coast.
Whether ascent per run starts building toward sustained climbing rather than the rolling profiles logged so far, given the mountain crossing.

history.headline: Yesterday's 5 km recovery jog at a notably low HR closes out a +35% volume block with efficiency intact.
watch_items: Whether the short nights this week extend into a run, since the training load is still being carried alongside them.
Whether pack-carry running appears soon enough to adapt to the 6-8kg load before the crossing.
Whether ascent per run starts shifting toward sustained climbing rather than the rolling profiles logged so far.
Whether easy-run HR holds at the lower band once the next hard session re-enters the schedule.

history.headline: Yesterday's easy 12 km sits cleanly in the lower HR band, holding the efficiency signal steady into a high-volume block.
watch_items: Whether the lower easy-run HR band holds once a genuinely hard session returns to the schedule.
Whether loaded pack-carry running appears soon enough to adapt to the 6-8kg demand before the crossing.
Whether sustained climbing starts replacing the rolling ascent profiles logged so far, given the mountain crossing ahead.
Whether the recent run of short nights extends further or settles back toward the block average.
